name: Mouse on Mars
label: Thrill Jockey
lede: Two friends from the Rhineland, by Wikipedia's account born on the same day in the same hospital, have spent three decades making electronic music that sounds like it's laughing with its own machines.

eras.title: Wibbly, barely digital
eras.text: Mouse on Mars started as two friends, Jan St. Werner from Cologne and Andi Toma from Düsseldorf, making wordless records out of krautrock, dub, techno and ambient for London's Too Pure. By the late '90s they had their own label, Sonig, and were in the studio with Stereolab.

years.h: Jan St. Werner and Andi Toma form Mouse on Mars
years.p: Childhood friends Jan St. Werner of Cologne and Andi Toma of Düsseldorf start a duo. Wikipedia says they were born on the same day in the same hospital.
Mouse on Mars' debut album. AllMusic's Sean Cooper called it a wibbly, barely digital match of ambient texture with techno, dub and krautrock.
years.xp: The first single, Frosch, came out on Too Pure the same year, and the duo landed a track on the Trance Europe Express 3 compilation. There were no vocals: early Mouse on Mars was all texture and rhythm.

years.p: Mouse on Mars' second Too Pure album is lighter and wider-ranging. A single that year was called Saturday Night Worldcup Fieber.
Mouse on Mars' third album for Too Pure. The same year Instrumentals comes out on Sonig, the duo's own label.

years.h: Mouse on Mars work on Stereolab's Dots and Loops
years.p: Mouse on Mars record and tour with [[Stereolab|f1df0431-9250-4ec8-95d8-f19ce7cf7fb6]], appearing on Dots and Loops and the Miss Modular EP. Jan St. Werner and [[Lætitia Sadier|9710d91f-bfbd-4f84-9c54-cb04f2a464b1]] have since sung karaoke duets together.
Mouse on Mars release Glam on Sonig, their own label, between the Too Pure years and the Thrill Jockey ones.

eras.title: Thrill Jockey, the first time
eras.text: Thrill Jockey picked Mouse on Mars up in America just as the duo brought live instruments into the machines. A touring drummer became a singer, the records turned toward pop, and a single remix led to a band with The Fall's Mark E. Smith.

years.h: Niun Niggung brings live instruments into the mix
years.p: Released by Domino and Sonig in Europe and Thrill Jockey in the US, Mouse on Mars' fifth album puts real playing up front for the first time.
Mouse on Mars keep pushing live instruments into the electronics. Thrill Jockey also issues the singles Actionist Respoke and, in 2002, Agit Itter It.
Mouse on Mars' most accessible record leans on vocals from touring drummer Dodo NKishi, the third member of the live band.

years.h: The single Wipe That Sound brings in Mark E. Smith
years.p: [[Mark E. Smith|35e5ce55-486d-40a4-9ab5-08de9be70d33]] of [[The Fall|d5da1841-9bc8-4813-9f89-11098090148e]] works with Jan St. Werner and Andi Toma on the Mouse on Mars single Wipe That Sound, their first collaboration.
Recorded with Mouse on Mars as a three-piece: St. Werner, Toma and Dodo NKishi on drums.
Mouse on Mars release Varcharz through Sonig and [[Mike Patton|6e891631-d99c-4768-8bc2-5e5feb42881c]]'s label Ipecac Recordings.

years.h: Mark E. Smith says he's been sacked from Von Südenfed
years.p: Mouse on Mars and Mark E. Smith release Tromatic Reflexxions on Domino as Von Südenfed. After two December 2007 shows were cancelled because of illness, Smith claimed he'd been sacked.
years.xp:
Critics compared Von Südenfed to [[LCD Soundsystem|2aaf7396-6ab8-40f3-9776-a41c42c8e26b]]; Smith pointed out that LCD Soundsystem were heavily influenced by the Fall. The singles were Fledermaus Can't Get It and The Rhinohead.

Despite the sacking talk, Smith played with them live again and said a second album was possible. Not enough was recorded before he died in January 2018.

eras.title: Monkeytown
eras.text: After six years without a Mouse on Mars album, the duo moved to Modeselektor's Berlin label Monkeytown, brought in singers, producers and a punk band as collaborators, and started building their own music software.

years.p: Mouse on Mars' first album in six years, and their first on Monkeytown, the label run by Berlin duo [[Modeselektor|8a7a4e72-a099-425f-8238-80706fc1c746]].

years.h: The WOW EP with Dao Anh Khanh and Las Kellies
years.p: Mouse on Mars' WOW EP on Monkeytown is a first recorded collaboration with singer Dao Anh Khanh, producer Eric D. Clark and punk band Las Kellies.

years.h: A Berlin Music Video Award for special effects
years.p: Mouse on Mars win Best Special Effects at the 2013 Berlin Music Video Awards.
The last Mouse on Mars release on Monkeytown before the move back to Thrill Jockey.

eras.title: Back on Thrill Jockey, with people and machines
eras.text: Returning to Thrill Jockey, Mouse on Mars went big: a 20-plus-guest ensemble record at footwork tempo, then an album about artificial intelligence that taught software to talk. Their own MoMinstruments apps and object-based spatial mixing were part of the kit.

years.h: Dimensional People: Bon Iver, the National and Swamp Dogg
years.p: Mouse on Mars' return to Thrill Jockey features [[Justin Vernon|0f1d5b01-8784-4870-9bd6-fa43178b9441]], [[Aaron Dessner|1890e726-4817-42f4-92e7-ca78bef6692a]] and [[Bryce Dessner|20336142-85de-4e11-a1fd-a6c815b4e583]], [[Swamp Dogg|1403fbec-11e3-4ccb-af25-d26c9a05bc9d]], [[Zach Condon|f358bc90-dcb9-4ecb-bac6-55d52ba755c9]], [[Lisa Hannigan|8d0d65cf-3d01-4110-bf36-7e1aa27b68f2]], [[Sam Amidon|2e088ea8-b8f7-4df4-ac83-7024a50aabf1]] and about 20 more.
years.xp: Most of it runs at 145 beats per minute, a tempo the duo took from Chicago footwork, inside one harmonic spectrum. It premiered as a spatial composition using object-based mixing, and was planned as an installation and performance as well as an album.

q: AI is capable of developing qualities that we attach to humans
years.p: Mouse on Mars build software that models human speech from the voice of writer Louis Chude-Sokei and DJ Rayne, then play it like a synth, with Dodo NKishi on percussion and art by Casey Reas.
years.xp: The duo worked with the AI collective Birds on Mars and former SoundCloud programmers Rany Keddo and Derek Tingle. The voice could be pushed faster or slower, happier or sadder. St. Werner argued that machines should be treated as collaborators, not competitors.

years.h: A collaboration with the late Lee "Scratch" Perry
years.p: Wikipedia lists Spatial, No Problem, a Mouse on Mars album with dub pioneer [[Lee "Scratch" Perry|af75ebe4-3ab1-423d-a499-2a6f9d011ce2]], who died in 2021, as a 2026 release on Domino.
